motivation: Amendment 15 fixed a three-round recovery budget. Every unrecovered arm resolved all three rounds and hit a fourth conflicting commit (Jsonpickle 6/6 per consumer; one Codex RO-Crate arm). This amendment asks whether those states are recoverable at all under a larger budget, so that budget-exhaustion and irrecoverability can be distinguished.

design.everything_else: identical to amendment 15 (same consumers, models, efforts, prompts, harness, verification, future session, strict evaluation)

outcomes: recovery success, rounds used, number of distinct conflicting commits, verified recovery, post-recovery continuation; reported as an extended-budget sensitivity next to the frozen three-round result, never substituted for it
amendment_15_outcomes_status: already opened; arm set fixed by the exhaustion event, not by any future outcome

revision_1.reason: Two Claude arms (jsonpickle-342 -> jsonpickle-469, low and high) ended with recovery_unresolved in round 5 because the Claude CLI returned 'You've hit your session limit' (account usage cap), not because the agent failed to resolve. No other Claude row in any experiment contains a limit message (scanned calibration, strict heldout, amendment 15, amendment 16).
revision_1.action: The two rows are quarantined in frontier_recovery_extended_claude.session_limit.jsonl and the two arms are re-executed under the identical protocol after the limit reset; only the re-executed rows enter the summary.
